question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched position within the Chinese Communist Party, secured through extensive power consolidation since 2012 and the 2018 removal of presidential term limits, underpins the 95.5% implied probability against his removal before 2027. No successor has been elevated to the Politburo Standing Committee, and recent analyses point to expectations of a fourth term beginning at the 21st Party Congress in 2027 amid limited internal divisions or visible challenges from party elites, the military, or society. The absence of major political shocks, leadership purges targeting Xi directly, or institutional pressures in the past year has reinforced trader consensus on continuity. While low-probability events such as sudden health developments, elite factional shifts, or significant external crises could still alter the trajectory, structural barriers including surveillance mechanisms and loyalist appointments make near-term exit highly unlikely.
